item.title: Kate Gosselin says her kids know who she ‘truly’ is as son Collin levels abuse allegations
item.description: Kate Gosselin responded to a fan on TikTok, saying her kids know who she "truly" is amid Collin Gosselin's abuse allegations and memoir release.
item.content:encoded:
Kate Gosselin says her children know who she "truly" is amid abuse allegations made by her son Collin.

The 51-year-old former reality star took to TikTok on Thursday to celebrate her boyfriend Steve Neild’s birthday, and got support from her fans in the comments section.

"Happy Birthday Steve ! Strength isn’t just about enduring—it’s about loving deeply enough to do what is right even when it costs you," one TikTok user wrote in the comments section. "Look at the beautiful life and happily ever after You have found now that You made sacrifices that no Mama should have had to make alone."

They continued: "When people attack You, it might sting for a moment, but it can never shake who You are. It only confirms that You stood your ground and remained true through it all. God is guiding You two."

‘JON & KATE PLUS 8’ STAR COLLIN GOSSELIN ACCUSES MOM OF TRYING TO ‘BURY’ HIM TO ‘PROTECT HER REPUTATION’

KATE GOSSELIN DEFENDS HERSELF AGAINST SON COLLIN AS HE PREPARES TO RELEASE SHOCKING NEW MEMOIR

Kate responded to the comment by thanking the fan, telling them, "I needed this encouragement and you are right," before adding that "I know who I am and my kids know who I truly am and to me, that’s all that matters."

The exchange came shortly after Collin alleged on "The View" that his sister Hannah felt compelled to say the two of them had not spoken in a year as a form of "damage control" for having participated in an upcoming Netflix documentary alongside Collin and their father.

In a statement, Hannah wrote that she has a relationship with her mother and other siblings, but has not "lived with my dad for over a year" and hasn't "spoken to Collin in close to a year." She added that she will not be making any more statements about "Collin's behavior growing up" or her experiences with him as a kid.

"All families are very complicated, and that statement sounded like a lot of the words of my mother, especially the last part. What I do believe has happened is that Hannah’s caught in the middle — and nobody deserves that," Collin said on "The View." "I know what it feels like to have to fight to have a relationship with your siblings. I don’t have one with my siblings, and I know how much that hurts. Not only is she caught in the middle, but I do believe my mom is either leveraging finances or Hannah’s relationship with our siblings over Hannah."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

He added that "Hannah opened up about a lot of truths" in the documentary and is "trying to do pre-damage control ... because my mom has placed that guilt on her," and that that is not fair for Hannah.

Collin recently opened up about the alleged abuse he endured while living with his mother in his memoir, "In the Shadow of Eight."

In the memoir, he accused his mother of restraining him with zip ties, hitting him when he failed to perform for cameras and isolating him in the family’s basement.

He first spoke out against his mother in a 2022 interview with Entertainment Tonight, when he alleged his mom sent him to live at the Fairmount Behavioral Health System – a psychiatric hospital located in Philadelphia – without telling anyone in the family when he was 12 years old. She said he was diagnosed with a behavior disorder, and she couldn't meet his needs.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Collin left the facility and moved in with his father, Jon, in December 2018, after Jon was granted custody. His sister Hannah also lived with their father at the time.

"I'd like an apology, simply put, an apology and for her to admit, and just take accountability for what she did," Collin told Fox News Digital earlier this month regarding his mother.

"And to say, you know, 'I'm sorry that I've soiled your name, and I've made every effort to bury you, to protect my reputation,' I think that'd be very honest and very powerful for her to say that … just show accountability because everything she's done to protect her reputation, it's all been at my cost."

Kate has previously denied allegations of abuse made by Collin.

item.title: Ole Miss and Texas collide in massive college football showdown with Arch Manning's season at stake
item.description: Ole Miss and Trinidad Chambliss face a struggling Texas squad as the line drops from -9.5 to -3.5 in this massive college football showdown.
item.content:encoded:
Last week was honestly one of the craziest weeks of football I’ve ever seen. College football was absolutely wild. It seemed like essentially every team in the top-10 of the national ranks lost. There was upset after upset, and a few teams were on the verge of stumbling as well. Week 7 saw a bunch of top ranked matchups, so naturally there were going to be losses from top teams.

This week doesn’t have nearly as many ranked matchups, but there is a massive one for Ole Miss and Texas.

Ole Miss comes into this game ranked 7th in the nation, and they own a 5-1 record. Their lone loss in the season was to Florida. That came after their biggest win of the season, when they beat LSU. It was one of the most obvious let-down situations in football. In the past two weeks, the Rebels have rebounded. They beat Vanderbilt 52-17 following the loss to Florida. Then last week, they took down Missouri. That was an even more impressive win as they beat the Tigers 31-3.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Rebels still own one of the better defenses in the country – even though they gave up 52 to Florida. Their quarterback, Trinidad Chambliss, has been about as good as you could hope for. He has four interceptions on the season, but only one of those came in the loss. He has a rushing touchdown in five of the six Ole Miss games. He has thrown for two or more touchdowns in five of the six games as well. Those are impressive numbers and he has made a big difference for the team. He will have a challenge against a good Texas defense, but the Longhorns have struggled.

Texas is arguably the most disappointing team in the country. They started the season once again with incredibly high expectations, but they fell apart. This is the last remaining game on the schedule that should be very difficult. I’m not trying to make excuses for the Longhorns, because their schedule has been tough, but with their talent, they shouldn’t have lost games, let alone back-to-back games.

OLE MISS DEFENSE TAKES CHARGE, SHUTS DOWN MISSOURI'S HIGH-POWERED RUSHING ATTACK IN 31-3 WIN

In the past two games, they lost both of them 27-24 to Oklahoma and Florida. Neither of those teams were ranked opponents, and both of the losses came in the state of Texas.

It seems almost unfathomable that the team could’ve lost both of these games. A lot of the blame is falling on Arch Manning, but I don’t know that it is fair to give him all the blame. Manning hasn’t been a difference-maker, but I also don’t think he has cost the team games. He has completed about 64% of passes with 11 touchdowns and five interceptions this season. He had two against Oklahoma, so maybe that one was his fault. He has been sacked 17 times in six games, but the blame really should be on the coach for having a poor game plan.

The line on this game has dropped significantly from the opening. Texas was a -9.5 favorite coming into this game when the lines opened. Now they are down to just -3.5. I don’t blame people for taking the points, and still think there is some value.

The Rebels have a good offense, and a solid defense. Still, when a season is on the line, and a team is at home, you kind of have to think they will put their best effort out there. It wouldn’t be at all surprising to see Steve Sarkisian fired if they lose this game. I do expect Texas to win, so the -160 isn’t a terrible look, but I think this will be a lower scoring game. I’ll back the under 54.5.

item.title: Death toll rises to 9 in church attack as officials blame 'extremist' Islamist ideology
item.description: Footage shows gunmen armed with pistols and a rifle storming a Greek Orthodox church in Karak during a funeral service, killing nine in Jordan.
item.content:encoded:
A group of gunmen stormed a Christian church in Jordan during a funeral on Friday, killing nine people and injuring more than two dozen, according to authorities.

The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 55 miles south of the capital, Amman.

Jordanian Health Minister Ibrahim al-Budour said Saturday that one critically injured patient remained hospitalized at Prince Ali Military Hospital in unstable condition.

Government spokesperson Mohammad Momani said Saturday that the attackers subscribed to "extremist takfiri ideology," which brands people who reject a strict interpretation of Islam as apostates or nonbelievers. Terrorist groups such as ISIS have invoked takfiri beliefs to justify killing Muslims, Christians and Jews.

BISHOP ROBERT BARRON: THE WAR ON CHRISTIANS IS REAL AND THE WORLD CAN NO LONGER STAY SILENT

Karak is home to a sizable Christian minority, and Momani sought to emphasize that Christians are "part of Jordan's national fabric."

It remains unclear whether the gunmen were affiliated with any terror group, and Jordanian authorities have not announced any arrests in connection with the attack.

Footage shown on Jordanian state television showed two gunmen armed with what appeared to be pistols approaching the church and opening fire, The Associated Press reported.

A third man carrying what appeared to be a semiautomatic rifle joined them moments later, before all three rushed toward the church.

TWO SUSPECTED GUNMEN DEAD, TWO IDF SOLDIERS KILLED IN WEST BANK SHOOTING

Photos and videos from witnesses show broken glass and pools of blood inside the church. After the location was secured by police, two bodies covered with blankets were seen outside the church.

Dorgham Halasa told the AP that intense gunfire erupted in the church some 15 minutes after the funeral service began. People began running, he said.

Halasa said he didn't see the gunmen, but said others he spoke with reported seeing at least four of them. Jordanian authorities had not confirmed the number of attackers as of Saturday.

On Friday, King Abdullah II said Jordan will "confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties."

"Whoever imagines that the bullets of treachery can divide the ranks of Jordanians will fail in his endeavor before our steadfastness and unity," he added. "Our deepest condolences to the families of the martyrs, and our wishes for recovery to the wounded."

Jordan announced three days of national mourning following the attack, according to the state-run Petra News Agency.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Stephen A Smith doubles down on Trump dinner, challenges critics by asking, 'What the f--- are you doing?'
item.description: Stephen A. Smith fired back at D.L. Hughley and other critics of his White House meeting with President Donald Trump, asking what they're doing for the community.
item.content:encoded:
Stephen A. Smith doubled down on defending his meeting with President Donald Trump during an episode of his "Straight Shooter" show on Thursday, challenging his critics by asking, "What the f--- are you doing?"

Smith said during the show he wanted to bring several issues to Trump's attention, but his top priority was to tell the president, "With the squashing of DEI initiatives, it's essentially had a different kind of effect. It's discouraged CEOs of corporations in the private sector to be philanthropic and charitable with their money and give to HBCUs because they're fearful it will be perceived as a DEI initiative being exercised by them."

"I needed the president to speak out against that, and he said he didn't think about that and that is something that he was going to tackle, not to mention the fact he followed up with a call to assure me that's exactly what he was going to tackle in a matter of days when he meets with these HBCU officials. Now I don't know what's going to happen, but I tried, as I always have and as I always will," Smith said.

Smith met with Trump, comedian Bill Maher and musician Kid Rock at the White House on Oct. 15.

JOY BEHAR WANTS TRUMP BACK ON ‘THE VIEW’ DESPITE SAYING HE’S ‘NOT LONG FOR THIS WORLD’

"All of these folks that are complaining about me showing up to the White House with Bill Maher, what the f--- are you doing? Have you done anything? Are you doing anything? I'm sorry for cussing. I don't mean to, apologizing to the executives at SiriusXM, but damn it. Sometimes we do stuff on the air that we do off the air. This is ridiculous. I mean, it's just, it's never enough," Smith argued.

Smith repeatedly criticized comedian D.L. Hughley during the show, after Hughley questioned Smith's meeting with Trump on the "Uncertain" podcast.

"Why is it that Trump feels so comfortable talking to you when he's shown an aversion to people that challenge him?" Hughley asked during the discussion, as he and his co-hosts criticized Smith for sitting down with the president. "If you challenge him, that's it. Why is it? It isn't that where Stephen A. Smith finds himself his positions, it is that why are people that have a disdain for us so comfortable around you?" 

"I think that it says something about you when the people who hate us like you," Hughley added. "Why is it the people that hate my heroes love you?"

Smith criticized Hughley over his comments, saying, "I'm sick and tired of people b----ing and moaning about what needs to be done in our community, but when somebody is actually trying to take steps to do something about it in our own small way, we selling out. We this, we that. What you doing? What you doing? It's a rhetorical question 'cause we know the answer ain't nothing but b----ing."

TRUMP ADMIN'S PUSH TO SCRAP DEI IN FEDERAL GOVERNMENT TAKES LANDMARK STEP WITH NEW HIRING RULE

Smith also defended his Trump meeting during an appearance on "The View" on Wednesday. He told the co-hosts he would not apologize for it.

Co-host Sunny Hostin asked Smith, "He has this history of racial bias that is so clear. Did you think meeting with him, that you got anywhere?"

"I don't know. We'll find out, but he’s the president of the United States, and I’ll be damned if I’m not going to try," he said. "And the reality is I’m just speaking from a constitutional perspective in that regard."

He repeatedly argued that Trump would remain in office until 2028 and that people needed to deal with it.

"You’re going to have to deal with him," he continued. "And when it comes to getting things done, I’m all about exhausting every means and every measure to try to do what’s in the best interest of our community. I’m not apologizing for that to anybody."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"Stephen A. Smith and Bill Maher, along with John Fetterman, are a dying breed of individuals who believe in the exchange of ideas and positions with those they all may disagree with, as exemplified by the recent dinner at the White House with President Trump and Kid Rock," Fox News contributor Joe Concha told Fox News Digital in a statement about Smith's remarks. "Unfortunately, the trend on the left is to shut down anyone through censorship or otherwise anything resembling debate."

item.title: Portland Thorns get destroyed in the comment section for praising fans on the same night XX-XY group attacked

item.content:encoded:

"Julie, a 57-year-old lesbian, was shoved down by a male @ThornsFC fan and tumbled over two rows of chairs. All for wearing an @xx_xyathletics shirt. He later apologized and said he didn’t know why he did it, he was just following the crowd. She has filed a police report," she reported on X with an accompanying video.

Other replies included:

WNBA WON'T NAME PERSON RESPONSIBLE FOR SECURITY INCIDENT OVER FANS' SHIRTS, AS DREAM BLAME LEAGUE

If this incident proved anything in my mind, it's that the NWSL is more radical and intolerant than the WNBA.

item.title: ‘80s pop star Taylor Dayne celebrates 4 years cancer-free after frightening diagnosis with no symptoms
item.description: Taylor Dayne opens up about her colon cancer journey, urging women to advocate for colonoscopies earlier as she prepares for her Las Vegas residency.
item.content:encoded:
Taylor Dayne has plenty of reasons to celebrate.

The pop star, known for the '80s hit "Tell It to My Heart," has been keeping busy gearing up for her first Las Vegas residency at Harrah's Las Vegas.

The Grammy-nominated artist, who announced in 2022 that she'd privately battled stage 2 colon cancer, said she's been given the all-clear and is ready to party with her fans.

TAYLOR DAYNE RECALLS FINDING FAME WITH ‘80S HIT ‘TELL IT TO MY HEART’: ‘I WAS PRAYING TO GET SIGNED'

"I've been cancer-free for four years now," she told Fox News Digital with a smile. "I've been on the path of being very ardent about taking care of my health and being on top of my colonoscopies. There are no guarantees in life, but especially as women, we need to advocate for our health and be on top of our checkups."

"I was already on top of my colonoscopies when I was told I had a lot of polyps," the singer said. "It was through a routine checkup that they found a very aggressive polyp. This is how quickly these things can escalate and really take a turn. But my mindset was, 'What do I do right now?' I was very much in action mode."

Dayne, who didn't experience any symptoms before her diagnosis, stressed that routine screenings are essential.

"I was 50 years old, and they said, 'Now's the time to go in for this,'" Dayne, 64, said. "It's not like that anymore, because of our food, our diets, what we're exposed to daily. You really have to think about your timeline earlier than we've ever done. And we have such high-paced lifestyles. Most people are busy working, busy being parents, busy just being out there juggling. We can't put our health on the sidelines."

The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force recommends that adults at average risk begin colorectal cancer screening at age 45, down from the previous recommendation of 50. People at increased risk, including some with a family history of colorectal cancer, may need to begin screening earlier.

"I thought it was a male-dominated disease, like prostate cancer," she said. "I was like, 'Colon?' It wasn't really resonating with me, and it certainly wasn't resonating with anyone in my family. I learned from my experience, be your own warrior, be your champion. And that's what I did. It started with me asking, 'Why do I keep developing polyps?' You have to be your own champion, your own voice in getting the information you need, the plan you need."

Dayne said her experience also taught her the importance of speaking up early. She noted that advocating for oneself can be harder when seriously ill.

"When you're that ill, there's very little that the person can do," she explained. "Your advocate is usually your partner, your spouse, your best friend. But oftentimes, it's just yourself. It made me realize a lot of things. And I'm so grateful, ever grateful. For me, it turned on a lightbulb, a desire to live, a desire to really push through things. And it's brought a lot of love to my heart because I've met so many people I otherwise wouldn't have met because we have so much in common now. Survivors."

Dayne's renewed focus on her health is also tied to her desire to be present for her children.

"Your kids don't think of you as having a career," she said. "They don't think about your fame, your awards, the guest house. All they want is for their needs to be met. You're just mom to them. I became a very different touring artist then. And touring was the largest component of my career. But I was a single parent. I raised them. I was then the mother bird who needed to always come back to her nest."

Dayne follows a no-nonsense health regimen that helps her look and feel her best as she prepares for her Las Vegas residency.

"I'm very religious with my morning ritual, whatever my morning looks like, because my morning could be one o'clock in the afternoon, and it could be five in the morning," she said. "I do my peptides. I do my collagen. I do my bone broth. I do copper for my skin. I want to be optimal. That takes stretching, Pilates, yoga, daily exercise. You have to take care of yourself spiritually, emotionally, mentally."

"It's a real juggle," Dayne continued. "But the first moment you have in the morning, the first two minutes you have, should be centering yourself. And then I do my tinctures. I also like to have a big ol' smoothie. I usually have just liquids in the morning. I also love soursop, especially when I travel. I have to have a healthy lifestyle to meet the demands of what it takes to be physically on stage every night."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Long before her health battle, Dayne experienced another life-changing moment — realizing just how quickly "Tell It to My Heart" had made her a star.

"I was in Munich preparing to make an appearance and I said, 'What are all these people doing outside? Why is their hair crimped? Why do they have red lips? Oh my God, they look like me,'" Dayne recalled.

"It's not overnight stardom because I spent 15, 16, 17 in every club conceivable in New York in the '80s," she said. "But when you have a single like that, the next thing you know, you're on 'Top of the Pops.' I just knew my life would never be the same. I had no idea people would love my music so much, that they would want to look like me. Here we are, 39 years later."

"I never said, 'This is going to last forever,'" she said, reflecting on her fame. "How could you ever know? It was a moment. I was young, I was 22, 23. You just want to catch the wind."

Nearly four decades into her career, Dayne sees her upcoming Las Vegas residency as a victory lap.

"This is the cherry on top and recognizing that after three decades in this business, my music is still the soundtrack of so many people's lives," she said. "I am honored. My health, my wellness, my family, I am grateful for it all."

item.title: Great relationships have 3 essential ingredients — and one factor that can ruin everything
item.description: Simon Sinek reveals his "3+1" formula for great relationships, breaking down why infatuation and dopamine spikes can send dangerously wrong signals.
item.content:encoded:
The difference between a good relationship and a great relationship could boil down to one formula.

Simon Sinek, author, inspirational speaker and founder of The Optimism Company in New York, shared his breakdown of core compatibilities for successful couples.

Sinek, who has built a following of millions with content about leadership and interpersonal communication, said he developed his "3+1" formula after years of considering what makes partnerships work.

5 MARRIAGE MISTAKES COUPLES MAKE WITHOUT REALIZING IT — AND HOW TO AVOID THEM

The formula centers on the following three core factors that can ebb and flow over the course of a partnership.

He also added a fourth bonus factor: circumstances.

Being intellectually compatible with your partner is essential, Sinek told Fox News Digital.

"You get along, you enjoy going out with them," he said. "It doesn't mean you're as smart as each other; it means you have something to talk about when you go out together."

COMMON MARRIAGE HABIT COULD QUIETLY KILL YOUR SEX LIFE, EXPERT WARNS

Emotional compatibility means being vulnerable and emotionally available to each other, while creative and sexual compatibility reflects enjoying intimacy with a partner.

Sinek said he groups sexual attraction and creativity together, as they use the "same part of the brain" that is imaginative.

"When people can bring imagination to their sex lives, that is creativity," he said. "You hear it in couples who have been together for 10, 15, 20 years – they talk about how things get stale, get boring. That's creativity."

A good relationship can blossom with one-and-a-half or two of these factors, according to Sinek, but a great relationship includes all three.

NEARLY 1 IN 3 MARRIED AMERICANS AREN'T HAVING SEX — EXPERT REVEALS HOW TO BRING BACK THE SPARK

"They're not all on high at the same time, so they sort of need each other to get through the relationship," he said.

The bonus factor – circumstances – is controlled by external forces and can tip the scales of a successful relationship, Sinek added.

"Sometimes, we meet somebody who fits all three, but they live on the other side of the world, and we can't move our lives and they can't move theirs," he said. "Or maybe they're already in a relationship and you shrug your shoulders and say, 'Bad timing.'"

"Sometimes we get infatuated because we find one or two of those things, but for it to really last, I’ve learned it takes all three, plus the circumstances."

Sinek warned that having one or two of these factors so highly developed, especially early in a relationship, can create the misleading impression that "this is my person."

"One of the biggest things I’ve learned about relationships is the danger of infatuation," Sinek said, noting that early attraction can be driven by dopamine rather than love at first sight.

He said people can fall for "the fantasy that the person represents" and think, "I’ve been looking for someone like you for my whole life," despite knowing someone for only a few hours.

After the initial infatuation fades, it may become more clear whether a person is a good long-term match, according to Sinek. He suggested that a lack of intense infatuation at the beginning could sometimes be a positive sign.

"You hear about people who knew each other for 10 years because they worked together," he said. "And then they finally realize that they're in love with each other. There was no infatuation. There was no spike."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Sinek encourages people to give potential partners who meet many of the desired criteria a chance, even if there isn't an immediate spark.

"I know I've made this mistake a million times," he said. "I met great people, but there was no infatuation, so I was like, ‘nope, not for me.’ Or I was seduced by the infatuation."

For committed or long-term couples who seem to have the core factors out of balance, Sinek urges them to pay closer attention to habits that may be pulling them away from the relationship.

"You see people who go out for dinner on a regular basis, and they are either on their phones the whole time, or they're looking in other directions," he said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Maybe somebody needs to put in an effort to say, ‘Let's put our phones away. Let's trade phones when we go out so we don't even have the temptation,’" Sinek suggested.

The expert reiterated that for those who want a lasting relationship — in a fast-paced dating climate that’s more sexually driven and tied to instant gratification — all three parts of the formula must develop.

"Even the sexual connection sometimes doesn’t happen at the beginning, and that also can come later," he said. Emotional connection can change the dynamic between partners, Sinek added.

He cautioned against placing too much importance on one or two factors simply because they are especially strong or appear early.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Sinek continued, "It’s recognizing that when they start to wax and wane, all three of them are going to matter and they’re going to show up naturally at some point, so it's more of an awareness rather than trying to force it."

item.title: Obama prepares to rally with Michigan Dem who once delivered scathing verdict on his presidency
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed rallies with Barack Obama in Michigan, but undecided Black voters in Detroit say the endorsement hasn't swayed their decision.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed is set to rally with former President Barack Obama on Saturday as Republicans raise questions about his support among Black voters, a crucial Democratic constituency in the battleground state.

Obama formally endorsed the Michigan Democrat earlier this month, filming a campaign ad that ran on Oct. 12 imploring his supporters "to support Abdul El-Sayed for the United States Senate." His upcoming rally with El-Sayed has become a major political event as the progressive Senate candidate continues his effort to build bridges with the Democratic Party’s establishment.

Obama's support has also renewed scrutiny of El-Sayed's past criticism of the former president, including a sharply worded 2012 essay accusing him of failing to deliver on the promises of his presidency. Conservatives have suggested that the El-Sayed campaign is leaning on Obama to build support among the African American community, whose turnout could be decisive on Election Day.

ROGERS ARGUES EL-SAYED IS VULNERABLE WITH 2 TRADITIONALLY DEMOCRATIC BLOCS AS OBAMA HEADS TO MICHIGAN

Claims that El-Sayed is only receiving lukewarm support from the Black community began during his primary race against Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens. El-Sayed performed strongly among Arab American voters during the Democratic primary, but he narrowly defeated Stevens after polls showed her attracting stronger support among Black Democratic voters. El-Sayed's uneven support among key Democratic constituencies has raised questions about his ability to unite the party's coalition heading into November.

Black voters are crucial to the Democratic coalition in Michigan. Low turnout or defections to the GOP in Michigan among African Americans could seriously endanger the Democratic Party’s path to control of the Senate.

OBAMA'S STAR POWER GETS A REALITY CHECK FROM BLACK VOTERS IN CRUCIAL SENATE RACE: 'IT'S A TURNOFF'

A poll conducted by Fox News Digital in late September found that just 77% of Black voters were supportive of El-Sayed, a figure well below where Democrats typically perform with the demographic.

It is unclear what impact, if any, Obama wading into Michigan’s Senate election will have.

Fox News Digital spoke with more than a dozen Black voters in Detroit about Obama's endorsement, finding mixed reactions that included skepticism among undecided voters and enthusiasm from others who already planned to support El-Sayed. While the undecided voters largely agreed that Obama was still a leader within the Democratic Party, they generally did not put much weight on the former president’s endorsement of El-Sayed.

"Honestly, it's a turn-off just because I've seen too many candidates use him just to manipulate the Democratic vote," Mercedes, one undecided Black voter, told Fox News Digital about Obama's endorsement.

MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS LEADERS MUST ADDRESS ‘UNPAID DEBTS’ TO BLACK COMMUNITIES

"What he's been able to do is from an image standpoint, as far as ‘hope,’ he drove the point there," another undecided African American voter told Fox News Digital. "But as far as really giving back to the community, minority owned businesses, and everyone across the board, I don't really think he really got there for me … he really hasn't swayed me one way or another."

Rita, an undecided Black voter who said she had recently been homeless, said that Obama’s endorsement would not move the needle for her as she prefers to do her own research on candidates.

Juanita, another Black voter who wasn’t sure how she would vote in November, told Fox News Digital that, "I don't want to be pushed to vote for him because somebody else is backing him."

Even some African Americans who voted early for El-Sayed said Obama’s backing didn’t mean much of anything to them.

SOCIALIST POLITICIANS ARE 'MORE RACIST THAN THE KKK,' SAYS BLACK DEM OFFICIAL URGING VOTERS TO DITCH EL-SAYED

"I think that a lot of people put more stock into who the person is than what he does … his yay or nay doesn't sway me either way," one such voter told Fox News Digital.

Undecided voters, however, had mixed feelings about El-Sayed’s changing position on Obama.

"Yeah, I don't understand how you can endorse somebody that was kind of the opposition when you were in office," Juanita told Fox News Digital. "I mean, that doesn't make sense."

"I think I see it as a flip flop, but I also see it as an opportunity to pretty much highlight those things and how he's actually changed and why their objectives may align now," another voter said. "You know, people's objectives change, their perspectives change."

‘DESTROYING THE AMERICAN WAY OF LIFE’: EL-SAYED’S POLITICAL ORBIT COMPLICATES EFFORT TO MODERATE HIS IMAGE

Others, however, pointed out that pivots like El-Sayed’s are nothing new in politics, pointing to the fact that Vice President JD Vance was once a staunch critic of President Donald Trump.

The controversy surrounding El-Sayed’s purported flip-flop on Obama can be traced back to a 2012 Huffington Post essay where he accused Obama of failing to live up to the progressive rhetoric he campaigned on.

"I realize that I have little hope because there has been less change," El-Sayed wrote. "But I have to say now what I’ve been holding in throughout his campaign and what I think all of us have to admit: Obama was not the right choice — he just wasn’t the wrong one."

He went on to criticize the then-president for perpetuating war, violating civil liberties and carrying out more deportations than any previous president.

The Michigan Democrat has since walked back some of those criticisms, noting that it is possible to disagree with someone while still admiring them and praising how Obama operated under the circumstances he inherited.

DEM INSURGENT TURNS ON THE CHARM WITH PARTY ESTABLISHMENT AS SCHUMER LEAVES BITTER FEUD HANGING

Some, however, don’t buy that explanation.

Conservative commentator Jason Rantz said on a CNN panel that El-Sayed was setting aside his criticisms of Obama because he was in a desperate electoral position and needed to "try to bring in black voters."

Others, however, don’t think El-Sayed has a problem with Black voters at all.

Kandia Milton, a government affairs professional with deep ties to Detroit's African American community, told Fox News Digital that conservative claims that El-Sayed lacks appeal to Black voters are misguided.

"The great thing about Abdul is that he's not new to Detroiters. … And so Detroiters, once they understand his background, understand what he stands for and all the things that he's done in the past, you see greater enthusiasm for his campaign and his candidacy for Senate," he said. "He has been very active in getting out into the community. In fact, tomorrow we have a public meeting with Abdul at our church. Where he will be speaking to the community around, you know, the issues that he stands on and stands firm on."

El-Sayed’s rally with Obama is slated to begin at 5:00 p.m. and will feature Democratic gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson and other Michigan Democrats. Attendees will be encouraged to cast early ballots in support of the Democratic ticket.

The El-Sayed campaign and representatives for the former president did not respond to requests for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Wednesday.

item.title: Hunters and ranchers enlisted in battle against spread of flesh-eating parasite
item.description: A hunter's elk kill in Pecos County revealed the first confirmed U.S. wildlife case of New World screwworm, as USDA urges ranchers to watch for signs.
item.content:encoded:
A flesh-eating parasite that can harm cattle was found in an elk in western Texas, prompting officials to ask hunters and ranchers to help stop its spread.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture said Wednesday that New World screwworm was found in an elk on a game ranch in Pecos County. A hunter reported the animal after killing it.

The USDA and the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department (TPWD) are conducting additional wildlife surveillance, while the Texas Animal Health Commission plans to modify an existing infested zone.

AMERICA'S BEEF SUPPLY SHRINKS AS CATTLE FARMER WARNS 'THE NUMBERS ARE JUST NOT HERE ANYMORE'

"Hunters and others who spend time outdoors near infested areas are often among the first people to encounter affected wildlife, making their observations especially valuable to surveillance and response efforts," the USDA said in a statement.

"As hunting seasons continue across Texas and other states, hunters are encouraged to stay alert for signs of NWS when observing, harvesting, or processing wildlife," it continued.

PRICE OF ONE GRILLING STAPLE REMAINS AT RECORD HIGH AS BEEF LOVERS ADAPT

It urged hunters to be on the lookout for visible maggots in wounds or body openings, open or enlarging wounds, foul-smelling injuries, and animals that appear weak or distressed, and to report anything suspicious promptly. Infection signs around the nose, mouth, ears, eyes or genital areas also warrant attention, the agency added.

The TPWD urged hunters to inspect harvested animals before field dressing or moving them, and to also look out for irritated or depressed behavior, loss of appetite, head shaking, a smell of decaying flesh or unusual isolation in animals.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

New World screwworm was eliminated from the U.S. decades ago, but the parasite has been moving north through Central America and Mexico, Fox News Digital previously reported. Last year, the U.S. halted livestock imports from Mexico to keep it out. The pause lasted more than a year, straining cattle supply and contributing to record-high beef prices. Reopening began in stages in August.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

In June, officials confirmed the parasite in a Texas calf. They later found it in other animals, including a horse and a dog.

The Texas elk was the first confirmed U.S. wildlife case in the current outbreak. "The partnership between TPWD biologists and local hunters and landowners expedited the identification and confirmation of this new detection," Texas wildlife division director Alan Cain said in a statement.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

New Mexico authorities also reported screwworm in a beef cow this week and established an infested zone around the animal. Animals within that zone must be inspected and, if necessary, treated before being moved.

The parasite is a threat to animal health and meat production, but the USDA says it does not affect food safety, according to reports.

In a June statement, the National Cattlemen's Beef Association also said it was working with its state partners to combat screwworm, and praised federal eradication efforts including expanded fly surveillance, cattle treatments and sterile-fly releases. Fox News Digital has reached out to the group for an update.

item.title: Omar’s deleted tweet could give clue on alleged brother marriage
item.description: A deleted 2013 Father's Day post by Ilhan Omar referred to her father as "Nur Said," a name similar to her ex-husband's, raising new questions.
item.content:encoded:
A deleted 2013 social media post in which Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., appeared to refer to her father by a different name has resurfaced as federal investigators examine questions surrounding her identity and immigration records.

"Happy Father’s Day to my aabo Nur Said, I am forever grateful to Allah for giving me the best father …," Omar wrote in the June 2013 post, which was deleted in 2019.

Several records, including a memorial post by the Congressional Black Caucus marking his death in 2020, refer to Omar’s father as "Nur Omar Mohamed." But the now-deleted X post has Omar calling him "Nur Said," a name that also appears similar to the name of her former husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi.

REP ILHAN OMAR'S IMMIGRATION HISTORY FACES NEW SCRUTINY AS FEDERAL INVESTIGATORS SUBPOENA RELATIVES

The congresswoman deleted the social media post the morning of Sept. 19, 2019.

An archived version of the post, first reported on by the Daily Caller in 2019, resurfaced after federal agents searched Omar’s Washington, D.C., residence on Oct. 12 as part of an ongoing criminal investigation into possible false statements on immigration and naturalization documents. Omar and her office have repeatedly denied allegations that her former husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, is her brother.

She has also denied wrongdoing amid the federal probe, which she has called a political attack.

Somali names generally consist of a person’s given name, their father’s given name and their paternal grandfather’s given name. The similarity between names alone does not establish a familial relationship.

A statement allegedly attributed to Omar’s spokesperson and recirculated online said "Nur Said" was her father’s childhood nickname and that he maintained a public page using the name. The statement also said the tweet was deleted because Omar and her family had received threats.

FEDERAL AGENTS SEIZE PHONE OF REP ILHAN OMAR IN RAID TIED TO IMMIGRATION FRAUD PROBE

Omar’s office did not respond Friday to Fox News Digital’s request for comment on the now-deleted social media post.

Omar’s father is referred to as "Nur Said" in some reports. For example, a New York Post story on his alleged military experience quoted Oxford University historian Mohamed Haji Ingiriis as calling Omar’s father "Nur Said."

Fox News has not independently verified that Omar's father's name is Nur Said Elmi Mohamed, his alleged name, not Nur Omar Mohamed.

In a statement to Fox News Digital on Thursday, a spokesperson for the congresswoman said Omar has "repeatedly and unequivocally denied" the "baseless, disgusting conspiracy theory" that she married her brother.

The spokesperson pointed to Omar’s interview Wednesday on MS NOW, in which she was asked whether her one-time husband may have been a "distant relative."

"Not to my knowledge," Omar replied.

Recent court documents related to the search warrant for Omar’s Washington, D.C. residence, first obtained by Fox News Digital, connected to the federal investigation identify Omar as "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, a.k.a. Ilhan Abdullahi Omar." The filing does not explain why the name appears in the document or establish that Omar used a false identity.

ILHAN OMAR CALLS TRUMP ‘CREEP’ AS PRESIDENT REVIVES ‘FAKE NAME,’ MARRIAGE ALLEGATIONS

Omar told Fox News Digital on Friday that her "real name" is "Ilhan Abdullahi Omar" and not "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi."

"Ilhan Abdullahi Omar, you know it," Omar told Fox News Digital when asked about her name. "It’s Ilhan Abdullahi Omar."

Omar’s marriage to Elmi ended in divorce in 2017. She later legally married Ahmed Hirsi in 2018.

Two people familiar with the investigation told Fox News Digital that "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi" may be Omar’s legal name. Omar’s office has disputed that characterization.

A former Minnesota federal immigration judge told Fox News Digital that if investigators prove Omar knowingly used a false name on federal forms, the conduct could be brought into question under the federal false-statements statute, 18 U.S.C. § 1001. Whether the statute applies would depend on the specific documents, the materiality of any alleged misstatement and the evidence of intent.

The Justice Department did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

Hannah Brennan contributed to this report.

item.title: 'SNL' Weekend Update anchor calls Republicans slurs, mocks Charlie Kirk in stand-up special
item.description: Michael Che's Netflix special opens with jokes about Charlie Kirk's killing and repeatedly uses the R-word to mock President Donald Trump and MAGA supporters.
item.content:encoded:
"Saturday Night Live" Weekend Update co-anchor Michael Che joked about Charlie Kirk's killing and repeatedly used the R-word while mocking President Donald Trump and his supporters in his new Netflix special, "Michael Che: Shot in Minnesota."

The new stand-up special was taped at the First Avenue music venue in Minneapolis. Che opened the show by saying he felt so good that he might get emotional.

"I feel like Erika Kirk on this stage. That’s no disrespect to the Kirks, by the way."

Che said he didn't know who Charlie Kirk was before the activist was killed, joking that he initially thought people were talking about "the dude from Star Trek."

A YEAR AFTER CHARLIE KIRK'S MURDER, SOME COMICS ARE CALLING OUT JOKES ABOUT HIS DEATH

"I was like, 'What? They shot Captain Kirk?'"

Che said he then watched the graphic video of Charlie Kirk's assassination to better understand what happened, saying, "I wish I did not see that s---."

"I don’t know if you saw," he told his audience, "but it’s f---ed up."

Che said the best explanation he had heard for why Kirk was killed was that "in this country, straight White Christian conservative men are being silenced." He recalled having a debate about the issue "with this r-----ed guy."

"I know you shouldn’t use that word, but, I do ... It’s because I still see them. I’ll stop saying it when I stop seeing it," he said.

He further defended his use of the slur, saying, "Ever since we stopped using the word 'r-----ed,' r-----ed people have taken over the world. I don’t think that s--- is a coincidence."

HASAN PIKER DEFENDS USING INCENDIARY TERMS LIKE 'INBRED' OR 'ZIONIST PIG' AGAINST OPPONENTS

Che said that if people still used the R-word, Trump never could have become president.

"He just kept getting stronger and stronger. Now, we can’t stop him ... I watched those debates. They never know what the f--- to say to that guy. They don’t got the language ... 'He’s unpresidential.' It’s like, 'No, he’s a r-----ed guy.'"

Che said the Minneapolis audience would know exactly what he was talking about, because every time he turns on the news, "Minnesota is fighting some group of r-----s."

"No, it’s important to say it. R-----ed meaning regressive. Bunch of motherf---ers trying to take all our rights away."

Che also called Trump a "r----- whisperer."

"That’s all politics is these days. Just r----- whispering."

He mocked Trump’s ability to appeal to supporters through red MAGA hats and simple messaging, attributing the popularity of the recognizable caps to the fact that "r-----ed guys love hats."

BROADCAST BIAS: FEMINIST FREAKOUT OVER SHANE GILLIS COMMENT IS THE REAL JOKE

The 'SNL' co-anchor said the president would have made a great kindergarten teacher because he knows how to talk to people who "don’t like to think that much." 

Che argued Americans do not take presidential politics seriously enough, suggesting that the country should have a list of potential candidates years in advance.

"If it’s the most important job in the free world, we still don’t know? There’s no list?" he joked.

"Right now, ESPN has a list of the top 500 high school quarterbacks in the country. But every four years, we end up in this f---ed up 'Would You Rather.'

"One n----- is 80, the other n----- is 80-er."

Che later shifted into personal material about aging, drinking, relationships, sex and fatherhood, closing by imagining God as an absent parent.

"I think God loves us. I think he just had us at a very young age. He realized he had more living to do. 'I gotta get the f--- out of here. Here, take this book. I’ll be right back.' I ain’t seen him since."

Fox News Digital reached out to Michael Che for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Aggressive tipping demands from costumed performers on the Las Vegas Strip have prompted a warning from local authorities.

Officials are reminding tourists that paying for street performances or character photos is never required, as FOX5 Las Vegas reported.

Digital messages began appearing on billboards along the Strip on Friday, Oct. 16, with a direct warning to tourists.

LAS VEGAS PRICES SQUEEZE EVERYDAY TRAVELERS AS POPULAR CITY EMBRACES EXPENSIVE MAKEOVER

"When watching performances or taking a photo, tipping is NOT required," the signs read, according to reports.

Clark County officials said the campaign is not intended to discourage voluntary tips, however.

The initiative specifically targets performers who coerce visitors for cash or falsely imply that tipping is mandatory, FOX5 said. 

"It negatively impacts the economic lifeblood of not just Clark County — but the entire state tax base is dependent on the Las Vegas Strip," Clark County Commissioner Michael Naft told FOX5.

Fox News Digital reached out to Clark County for further comment.

The new warnings arrived after a tipping dispute involving costumed showgirls on the Strip allegedly turned violent.

Two visitors from North Carolina stopped for photos with three women dressed as showgirls outside Planet Hollywood on Sept. 30 and paid a $20 tip, Fox News Digital previously reported.

After the tourists began walking away, performer Jennifer Ortiz allegedly followed them and demanded between $60 and $180 for the photos, according to an arrest report.

The confrontation escalated into a fight that left both tourists injured.

Police said one visitor was struck more than 22 times and suffered a nearly 2-inch cut to the forehead after Ortiz allegedly hit the person with a high-heeled boot.

Ortiz and another performer, Magdellena Romero, were arrested.

Ortiz was charged with battery and obtaining money under false pretenses involving less than $1,200, while Romero was charged with battery.

The push to address tipping pressure has since drawn reactions from both travelers and Las Vegas residents online.

"Good, it is getting a little crazy," one Reddit user wrote. "I am glad they are clamping down after that brawl a couple of weeks ago."

Another commenter claimed aggressive tipping demands have been an issue for years, recalling seeing costumed performers pressure tourists for money.

Some users also offered their own thoughts for avoiding uncomfortable encounters with performers.

"Best advice is not to engage them," one commenter advised.

item.title: Bob Saget's widow Kelly Rizzo says his sudden death changed how she loves new boyfriend
item.description: Kelly Rizzo shares the last text Bob Saget ever sent her and how Breckin Meyer has embraced his memory as their relationship grows stronger.
item.content:encoded:
Kelly Rizzo isn't sweating the small stuff when it comes to love.

Nearly five years after the sudden death of her husband, Bob Saget, Rizzo is approaching relationships differently. The 47-year-old told Fox News Digital that she and her boyfriend, Breckin Meyer, have never had a fight in more than three years together — an outlook shaped by the sudden loss of her husband.

Rizzo hosts the podcast "Comfort Food with Kelly Rizzo," on which she sits down with celebrity guests and friends to discuss grief, coping and family.

SANDRA BULLOCK SAYS BRYAN RANDALL WAS ILL FOR 'HALF OF OUR RELATIONSHIP' AS SHE OPENS UP ABOUT HIS DEATH

"It's been over three years, and I don't want to jinx it, but we have never had a fight," Rizzo told Fox News Digital. "We've never been in a fight. And I think, at least from my end, it's because I don't ever want to have a day where we're fighting and, God forbid, something happens, or where we're fighting, and he feels upset or sad because I never want to hurt his feelings."

"I just don't do a lot of the things that maybe I would have done in the past or if I was a little bit more immature," she said. "That's really what this dating journey has taught me about myself."

Rizzo met Saget on social media in 2015, and they married three years later. On Jan. 9, 2022, the "Full House" star died at age 65 from accidental head trauma. Rizzo later found love again with Meyer, an actor. The couple made their public debut at Steven Tyler's annual Grammy Awards viewing party in February 2024, according to People magazine.

WATCH: KELLY RIZZO SHARES HOW BOB SAGET'S DEATH CHANGED HER DATING LIFE

"I've learned that it's so important to appreciate every single minute that you have with somebody because you don't know how much time you're going to get with them," Rizzo said. "You don't know how much time you're here on this Earth. So I'm so much better today at not sweating the small stuff."

"I don't pick little fights," she continued. "You know, let's test him to see how much he loves me. I just don't do any of that anymore. I think a level of maturity also comes with my age and just having been in relationships in the past. But because I lost Bob so suddenly and so quickly, I know what a gift every single day is."

Rizzo said she learned the importance of expressing love from Saget during their marriage.

"He always said, 'I love you. Tell everyone you love them,'" Rizzo said. "He was hugging people constantly. He was telling people ‘I love you.’ He never left a conversation without saying 'I love you' or leaving anything on the table. Everyone knew how he felt about them after every conversation or after every visit. And that was such a big lesson he taught people, even to this day. Even after almost five years."

Rizzo said opening her heart to someone new brought feelings of guilt, which she discussed on her podcast.

"I was always so concerned, like, 'If people know that I love Breckin now, are they going to think I love Bob less?'" she said. "What I've learned is that it's just absolutely not true. ... You can have 100% of love for the person you lost and still have 100% of your love for the person in your life now. And having the new person does not take away the love from the person before, from the person who passed away, because they can live together and coexist so beautifully and so simultaneously."

"My love for Bob today, it's a little different than it was when he was here, but it's not any less," Rizzo said. "So, I think that's a big misconception. People are worried that if they move forward, it means that either they're going to somehow forget the person who passed away, or that people will think that they love the person less."

Rizzo previously said she sought the blessing of Saget's daughters, with whom she remains close. Saget had three daughters — Aubrey, 39, Lara, 37, and Jennifer, 33 — with his former wife, Sherri Kramer.

"It's truly the biggest gift I could ever have dreamed of, because they're such angels," she said of her relationship with her stepdaughters. "We've just still been a family. I talked to Aubrey today for an hour and every conversation ends with 'I love you.' I'm going to see her tomorrow with my new step-granddaughter. It's just the biggest gift. I can't imagine doing this without them. And I don't want to put words in their mouth, but they've said the same."

"It makes me appreciate it so much more, because I see there are so many families, especially stepfamilies, similar to mine," Rizzo said. "They do not have this beautiful of a situation after someone's passing. So we know every day how unbelievably blessed we are that we have this relationship."

While Rizzo is moving forward, her love for Saget remains constant. When asked about her favorite memory of him, she recalled their last Christmas together in her hometown of Chicago.

"I remember he got to spend time with my nieces, one who was just born two weeks before," Rizzo said. "I remember he took this photo with my niece, Alexandra, at the dinner table. The last text that Bob ever sent me right before he passed away ... we were saying our goodnights, but when I woke up in the morning, I had a text from him that was that picture of him hugging my niece on Christmas."

"It was a little, I don't want to say odd, but a little different. It's not necessarily a text that I would've expected to get from him, this mushy picture. But I look at that as so significant because he and my niece had a special connection. And the fact that that was the last text he ever sent me was really special."

Rizzo said Meyer has also embraced Saget's memory, something she appreciates as their relationship continues.

"[I remember] my episode with Breckin, where Breckin is talking about how much he loved Bob and how much he respected him," she said. "I always joke that Breckin's the only person on Earth who Bob wouldn't be that mad about. He wouldn't love it, but he'd like him more than any other option."

Looking ahead, Rizzo is determined to embrace the future while honoring Saget's memory.

"I'm so grateful that I got to share my life with Bob and [I'm just] so grateful that I got to be in his world, understand him and help him feel understood, really, almost for the first time in his life," she said. "[I just put] in my head from almost day one that I'm not going to let this break me. I'm going to be OK."

item.title: 'Save Women’s Sports' activists ejected from NWSL match after being struck, confronted by pro-trans crowd
item.description: XX-XY Athletics supporters say they were physically struck before getting escorted out of a Portland Thorns NWSL game after unveiling a "Save Women's Sports" banner.
item.content:encoded:
Around 20 "Save Women's Sports" activists wearing XX-XY Athletics shirts were forcibly escorted out of a Portland Thorns match on Friday night after members of the group were struck and verbally berated by other fans during a demonstration supporting female-only sports.

The confrontation occurred during the Thorns’ match against the North Carolina Courage at Providence Park in Portland, Oregon. The club’s schedule designated the match as its "Fan Appreciation" night.

According to a preliminary account, the group entered with their XX-XY shirts covered and kept them concealed through the first half. At the start of the second half, they revealed the shirts and unfurled a large banner reading "Save Women’s Sports," but matters quickly escalated from that point on.

FANS DISAGREE WITH PORTLAND THORNS OVER REASON FOR EJECTION IN XX-XY APPAREL DISPUTE: 'THEY ARE LYING'

Other spectators, described in the account as supporters of transgender inclusion in women’s sports, allegedly responded with verbal abuse and physical aggression, including striking members of the group with flagpoles carrying trans flags. Security subsequently escorted the roughly 20 demonstrators out of the stadium.

The organizers included women’s sports activist Amy Sousa and commentator Brandi Kruse, who previously helped organize rallies supporting WNBA player Sophie Cunningham.

Sousa told OutKick that she and other XX-XY Athletics attendees filed police reports after being escorted out of the stadium.

"We were attacked by fans. We were hit with flags. We had drinks and thrown at us," said Sousa, standing behind police outside the stadium because she did not feel safe. "Other people were forcibly pushed out the door. We had an ADA woman in a walker, she was forcibly pushed out the door. They let these people hit us with flags, another woman was punched in the face, all because we wanted to stand there in our shirts to protect girls sports."

This wasn't the first time Sousa and XX-XY Athletics supporters had been ejected from a Thorns game at Providence Park. A smaller group was removed in early September, when Sousa said she was accused of being "transphobic" for her pro-women apparel.

WNBA FANS RECALL EJECTION THREAT OVER XX-XY ATHLETICS SHIRT AT FEVER-DREAM GAME: 'I WAS FLABBERGASTED'

The decision to unfurl the "Save Women's Sports" banner and reveal their shirts at the start of the second half Friday was strategic. Sousa hoped the group could avoid ejection because soccer has no official breaks in play. But members of the Rose City Riveters — the Thorns' emphatically pro-trans supporters group — appeared to have caught wind of their intentions.

Just before the second half began, a number of fans were given transgender pride flags, apparently in an effort to obstruct other spectators' view of the banner and XX-XY supporters. One man sitting across the aisle from the group repeatedly shouted, "F--- you! F--- you, scum!" Chants of "Trans lives matter!" followed.

OutKick reporter Matt Calkins, who was credentialed for the match, attempted to document the confrontation but was also subjected to verbal and physical aggression. He was flipped off, called a Nazi, had his phone knocked out of his hand and had beer poured on his neck. The interaction was captured by Calkins on video.

XX-XY attendees weren't treated much better. Kruse had her right arm restrained behind her back by a security guard, who walked her up the stairs to the concourse and out of the stadium. This happened after she said she and others were hit multiple times with flags, with the assaulters repeatedly acting like it was an accident. Kruse added that another XX-XY attendee was pushed over her seat and "tumbled down." Aside from one man who poured beer on someone, Brandi said no other assaulters were removed.

"I asked the security guard 'Why are we being asked to leave and they're not not being asked to leave?' If you want all of us to leave that's another thing, but just us? So I said 'I'm not leaving on my own accord'," Kruse said. "So two security guards grabbed me and took me out. I'm in shock over it."

TRANS ACTIVISTS HARASS, HURL SLURS AT SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS BEFORE FEVER GAME IN MINNESOTA

A separate security guard also yanked an Calkins' credential from around his neck as he interviewed Sousa. The guard returned it seconds later but declined to explain his actions when questioned.

Director of security Jim McCausland was texted for comment, per OutKick's request, but said he did not have time to talk. OutKick also reached to the Thorns' communication director for comment — specifically as to why XX-XY attendees were escorted out but not their assaulters — but received no response.

Roughly half a dozen XX-XY supporters left the stadium before the banner was even revealed, fearing for their safety after seeing spectators wearing "Protect Trans Kids" shirts featuring images of knives. But Ari Laureano, who has detransitioned, chose to stay.

Laureano said just after he unbuttoned his coat to reveal his XX-XY shirt, he was smashed in the face by a flagpole. He added that assaulters used flags as a barricade to hide that they were striking the women he was with.

Worth it to try and make a change? In Laureano's mind, yes. But he doesn't expect much sympathy from journalists.

"I think the average person looks at this and doesn't understand what's going on, and the media goes and calls all these women horrible homophobic bigots," Laureano said. "But I'm here with them as a gay man who was harmed by being transitioned young, and I'm being beaten alongside of them. These are just normal impacted women who care about women's sports."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

The National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) — which comprises the Thorns and 15 other teams — but like the WNBA, the league doesn't have a policy that would automatically exclude a male-born player.

Additionally, Washington and Colorado have measures on their Nov. 3 ballots that would restrict participation in school sports based on biological sex. Washington's initiative applies to K-12 athletics, while Colorado's would extend to college sports.

Women such as Sousa and Kruse — along with XX-XY founder Jennifer Sey — have been resolute in trying to get those measures passed. They've just never considered violence or vitriol as among their tactics.

"It's just fascinating this difference. Like, I live in Seattle, you know, as a conservative, I'm surrounded by things I don't like all the time — signs, ideas. It's never even crossed my mind to assault someone," Kruse said. "The mentality is very different."

item.title: Trump's war on drug cartels could gain powerful new ally after pivotal election
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro says Brazil would join Trump's Shield of the Americas anti-cartel coalition if brother Flávio Bolsonaro wins the Oct. 25 runoff.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: Brazil could join the U.S.-led effort to combat drug cartels if presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro wins the country’s Oct. 25 runoff election, according to his brother, Brazilian politician Eduardo Bolsonaro.

The initiative, known as the Shield of the Americas, is designed to expand security cooperation among countries in the Western Hemisphere, including intelligence sharing, military coordination and joint efforts to disrupt cartel financing.

The coalition follows the Trump administration’s decision in February 2025 to designate eight major criminal organizations as both Foreign Terrorist Organizations and Specially Designated Global Terrorists. The groups include Tren de Aragua, MS-13, the Sinaloa Cartel, the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, the Northeast Cartel, the Gulf Cartel, La Nueva Familia Michoacana and Carteles Unidos. 

LATIN AMERICA’S CONSERVATIVE SHIFT FACES ITS BIGGEST TEST YET IN BRAZIL ELECTION

"The main thing that we need to do is fight the cartels," Eduardo Bolsonaro told Fox News Digital. "They work together in a lot of countries, so we should fight back then."

Brazil has not joined the initiative under left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Eduardo Bolsonaro said that if his brother’s conservative Liberal Party wins the presidency, Brazil would work with the Trump administration to combat the country’s powerful criminal organizations.

‘DONROE’ DOCTRINE AND CONSERVATIVE VICTORIES SQUEEZE CARTELS IN LATIN AMERICA

"So I’m sure that, under the leadership of President Trump and the Shield of the Americas, we have the opportunity for the first time" to work together against the cartels, Eduardo Bolsonaro said.

Brazil’s presidential runoff will pit Flávio Bolsonaro against Lula after Bolsonaro led Lula in the first round. He has said he would seek closer security cooperation with the United States and other conservative governments in the region. 

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION CRACKS DOWN ON BRAZIL'S BIGGEST DRUG GANGS WITH ‘GLOBAL TERROR’ DESIGNATION

The potential addition of Brazil would expand the coalition’s presence in South America, where criminal groups such as Primeiro Comando da Capital and Comando Vermelho have become major forces in the regional drug trade.

Other countries participating in the U.S.-led effort include Argentina, El Salvador and Peru. The initiative has also drawn participation from countries including Ecuador, Panama, Paraguay and Chile, according to the State Department.

DRUG CARTEL KINGPIN AMONG TARGETS IN SWEEPING TRUMP CRACKDOWN ON ALLEGED MEXICAN CORRUPTION NETWORK

The coalition’s broader goals include combating drug trafficking, disrupting criminal financing and strengthening cooperation among law enforcement and military officials.

U.S. officials have repeatedly linked cartel activity to the trafficking of fentanyl and other illicit drugs into the United States. Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., has also attributed hundreds of thousands of American deaths to cartel-linked drug overdoses.

item.title: College football's NIL and transfer portal chaos on display as nation's top receiver holds absurd ceremony

... that he's signing BACK with the Beavers for next season.

"What is the major announcement you want to make to the country?" the CBS fellas ask Legree, who is stationed at St. Francis Academy with what sounds like a big crowd on hand.

"I will be signing with the Oregon State Beavers for the 2027-2028 season," Legree, who currently plays for the OREGON STATE BEAVERS, said.

Sadly, it's not.

And by the way, this has nothing to do with Jesse Legree, the player. He's arguably the best wide receiver in the country not named Jeremiah Smith.

The freshman currently leads the nation in receiving yards (1,040), touchdown catches (14) and yards per game (148.6). Not bad! It's only natural that folks would speculate that he's probably hitting the portal next season and going to an LSU, or Notre Dame, or Miami, or Ohio State.
